text:
maria (support): Customer ACME reported spikes in generation latency, p95 up from 220ms -> 980ms and p99 ~2.1s since yesterday afternoon. They see timeouts from our API and are threatening to cut over.
ajay (oncall): ACK. Any tracer links or request IDs? :eyes:
maria (support): Posted the example request IDs in the ticket: req_8s3a, req_8s3b. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/latency?svc=inference&from=01:00&to=now
oncall-bot: Alert fired: service.inference.p99 > 1.5s in prod (region: us-west-2). Count: 412 in last 15m.
sam (runtime): Looking at the logs for req_8s3a — lots of KV-cache misses + sudden increase in seq_len for that user (~2048). Could be a workload regression (long prompts).
lee (infra): Autoscale didn't spin extra pods last hour because queue depth threshold stayed low - suspect the long-tail single-request concurrency is causing head-of-line blocking on some GPU instances.
ajay (oncall): Immediate mitigations we can try: 1) circuit-breaker for clients hitting >X concurrent tokens; 2) fall back heavy requests to smaller model (quantized/or half-kv) or route to secondary region; 3) temporary per-key soft rate limit. Which is fastest?
sam (runtime): Fastest: deploy a route rule to fallback_model: 'redwood-small-q4' for requests with prompt_len > 1024. I can flip that in the routing config in ~10m. Also enable aggressive prefix caching for popular prefixes.
lee (infra): I can add a short-lived token-level limiter: rate_limit_tokens=2000/min for offending keys (maria can provide client API keys). That will reduce token storming and buy time for autoscale.
maria (support): I'll ask ACME for reproduction steps and client keys, and put their keys in the escalation doc. Sending keys now.
ajay (oncall): Plan: (A) immediate: apply token limiter for ACME + route >1024 to small-q4. (B) medium: enable circuit breaker at p99>1.2s with automatic failover to small-q4. (C) followup: root-cause — eval kernel/kv-cache cold start and add a buffering worker or adjust batch/window.
sam (runtime): I'll open a quick PR to routing-config and add the model-fallback rule. Will monitor p95/p99 in the next 15m. :thumbsup:
lee (infra): I'm kicking off a manual scale-up for us-west-2 to add 4 GPUs and increasing per-instance concurrency cap to avoid HL blocking. If that doesn't help, we rollback recent model change from yesterday's deploy (deployed by dev-sam).
ajay (oncall): dev-sam, did we push any model/serving changes yesterday that could affect long prompt handling?
sam (runtime): dev-sam is OOO today but I can check the deployment diff — we changed kernel selection heuristics to favor fused kernels on 2048 lengths. Might regress when combined with specific quantization path.
ajay (oncall): OK act as if we might rollback. Maria, tell ACME we have temporary limits to stabilize while we investigate and offer prioritized support window. Use canned message: "We're applying targeted rate limits and fallbacks to stabilize your requests; will update in 30m."
maria (support): Sent. ACME acknowledged and agreed to the 30m window. They provided a few more failing request IDs.
oncall-bot: Metric update: p95 -> 420ms (down), p99 -> 1.05s (down) after routing change. Keep observing for 30m.
ajay (oncall): Good. Next steps: monitor for regressions, if p99 rises above 1.5s we execute circuit-breaker and start rollback. Sam/Lee to prepare rollback steps and post them here. I'll update the incident tracker.
sam (runtime): Rollback checklist: 1) revert routing & kernel heuristics PR id #4821; 2) redeploy canary to 10% then 100% if clean; 3) ensure KV-cache prewarm for hot prefixes. I have scripts ready.
lee (infra): Infra checklist: 1) keep extra GPUs for 45m; 2) monitor queue depth and GPU utilization; 3) be ready to reimage instances if a kernel-level hotloop appears.
ajay (oncall): Thanks team. Reactions: :rocket:. I'll close thread if metrics stable for 30m.
